id_and_class.summary: Sam Coleman holds that the intrinsic nature behind the structure physics describes is made of qualities, the same kind of thing as redness or painfulness, but that these qualities are not in themselves experienced by anyone. Phenomenal consciousness occurs only when a brain becomes aware of organized qualities, which Coleman explains with his quotational higher-order thought theory. Qualities are irreducible and fundamental, while subjects and awareness are reducible.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as Awareness of Unexperienced Qualities

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is a relation of awareness to qualities. A quality is only the possible content of an experience; experience occurs when a subject's awareness takes it up.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Physical dispositions supervene on fundamental qualities and physical laws stay intact; Coleman calls this an ‘enriched form of physicalism.’ The qualities we experience are the very qualities that make up physical reality, experienced only contingently.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Weak emergence (qualities are fundamental, but awareness, and so experience, is a non-fundamental, broadly functional relation found in humans and other animals)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Subjects are reducible: a brain's higher-order architecture selects, unifies and bounds a set of qualities as one subject's experience. Coleman denies there are micro-subjects and insists that experience is always for a subject.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Qualia exist unexperienced throughout nature and are irreducible; ‘something it is like’ is a quality being displayed to a subject. Coleman calls qualities the really hard problem.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Intrinsic qualities as the categorical ground of physical dispositions, brains with higher-order representational architecture, and awareness as a cognitive relation.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Acquaintance: on the quotational view the quality one is aware of is part of the state of awareness itself, so it is presented rather than represented.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Two factors: organized qualities, and an awareness-conferring structure (a higher-order state) that frames some of them as the contents of one field of consciousness.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal consciousness, subjectivity, unity and boundaries of experience, acquaintance, and unconscious mentality.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Quotational higher-order thought: a higher-order state quotes a first-order quality, much as a gallery frame displays a painting, so the quality itself is presented. A quoted quality is conscious and an unquoted one is not.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Qualities pervade all of physical reality; experience exists only in organisms whose brains implement awareness of qualities.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Qualities are causally and metaphysically fundamental, since physical dispositions supervene on them. Coleman argues that denying unconscious mental qualities would threaten the causal power of conscious ones.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Qualities targeted together by one higher-order state belong to one field of consciousness; Coleman suggests a single very large higher-order state at each moment. A holistic ‘quality fabric,’ perhaps modeled by fields or entanglement, may be necessary but not sufficient for unity.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Mentality is an organized ‘Russellian harmony’ of qualities in the brain, some conscious and some not, which lets one account cover both conscious and unconscious beliefs, emotions and imagery.
core_claims_and_evidence: Subjects cannot sum: each viewpoint is exclusive and bounded, so many micro-subjects cannot compose one macro-subject, and micro-subjectivity is an idle wheel.
Qualities, unlike subjects, can combine and co-locate, so panpsychists should keep fundamental qualities and drop fundamental subjects.
A wholly non-qualitative ontology cannot intelligibly yield the qualitative character of experience.
Apparently separate sensory modalities may be regions of one larger quality-space, so a rich basis of qualities could generate all familiar qualities by recombination.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical, largely a negative argument from the combination problem.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Chalmers objects that reducing awareness leaves out the phenomenology of awareness itself; Coleman doubts such phenomenology exists. Mihálik argues an explanatory gap remains for our intimate access to qualities, and Rosenberg argues the quotational view wrongly moves worldly qualities into the subject and proposes a first-order version instead.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: The grain problem, how heterogeneous micro-qualities yield smooth macro-qualities like a visual field, remains a possible defeater that Coleman addresses with ‘mental chemistry.’ Whether higher-order structure explains awareness or merely correlates with it is open; Coleman also stays open to a non-reductive account of awareness such as sheer acquaintance.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: The view claims Russellian monism's advantages (no brute emergence of quality, no dualist causation) without filling nature with subjects; the cost is the hard-to-grasp idea of qualities that no one experiences.

AI_consciousness.rationale: All matter is qualitative and awareness is a functional relation, so it follows from the view that an artificial system would be conscious if it implemented awareness of qualities in the right way.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Qualities persist, but subjects and experience depend on a brain's awareness structure, so it follows from the view that a person's experience ends with it.
